title: Rolling across a surface

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions or on-screen text indicate slow motion; motion appears as real-time animation.

subjects.description: small round red object initially sitting on the dark block at the left edge

observation.what_happens: A red ball starts on top of a dark block at the left edge and travels rightward across the brown surface to the far right edge. The motion starts when it leaves the block and ends when it arrives at the far right and stops.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: x grows almost linearly near 980 px/s while y rises to 186 px near 0.48 s then falls, looking like a parabola but seen as rolling over a brown hump. Flight laws fit the parabola simply, while hump-constrained rolling laws explain y as hill shape H(x) and can level to zero and stop at the far edge.

law.title: Projectile flight, no drag
law.summary: The ball flies like a thrown rock with steady sideways speed and steady downward pull.

fitted.title: Projectile flight, no drag
fitted.summary: The ball flies like a thrown rock with steady sideways speed and steady downward pull.

candidates.ifItWins: The ball was actually airborne after leaving the block and y is free fall, the rolling appearance is just travel over a background.

law.title: Projectile with linear air drag
law.summary: The ball flies but air drag gently brakes it in proportion to speed.

fitted.title: Projectile with linear air drag
fitted.summary: The ball flies but air drag gently brakes it in proportion to speed.

candidates.ifItWins: Flight is right but air slows the ball, so the fall is asymmetric and the range is shortened.

Scale is in pixels with no real size so gravity is not Earth-like
critique.finding: The ball flies like a free projectile, keeping steady sideways motion while falling with pull {g}. No air drag is needed to explain its path.
critique.headline: Red ball sails freely with gravity alone
critique.why_it_won: It follows the bend in the path cleanly while adding drag only adds wobble without helping.

headline: Red ball sails freely with gravity alone
finding: The ball flies like a free projectile, keeping steady sideways motion while falling with pull 1530 ± 1.3 px/s². No air drag is needed to explain its path.

eyeball.law_in_words: Assuming vertical free fall from rest, drop distance delta_y = 0.5*g*t^2, so g = 2*delta_y / t_fall^2 estimated from pixel drop of the red ball from its support to the floor and fall time in the video.

clock.note: Gravity came out 160× too strong: the clip probably plays about 12× faster than real life (time-lapse or dropped frames).
